p: This was a certain tune of an instrument.
Of that perfect love that ought to be between the husband and the wife.
fairer than the children of men: Solomon's beauty and eloquence to win favour with his people, and his power to overcome his enemies, is here described.

ride prosperously because of truth and: He alludes to them, who ride in chariots in their triumphs, showing that the quiet state of a kingdom stands in truth, meekness and justice, and not in worldly pomp and vanity.
throne: Under this figure of this kingdom of justice is set forth the everlasting kingdom of Christ.
anointed thee with the oil of: Has established your kingdom as the figure of Christ, which is the peace and joy of the Church.
whereby they have made thee glad: In which the people made you joyful to see them give thanks and rejoice for you.
queen in gold of Ophir: Though he had many king's daughters among his wives, yet he found Pharaoh's daughter best.
Hearken: Under the figure of Pharaoh's daughter, he shows that the Church must cast off all carnal affections to obey Christ only.
daughter of Tyre shall be there: He signifies that many of those who are rich will be benefactors to the Church, although they do not give perfect obedience to the Gospel.

within: There is nothing feigned or hypocritical but she is glorious both within and without: and even though the Church has not always had this outward glory, the fault is to be imputed only to their own ingratitude.
children: They will have greater graces than their fathers.
in all the earth: He signifies the great compass of Christ's kingdom, which will be sufficient to enrich all his members.
name to be remembered in all: This must only be referred to Christ and not to Solomon.
